nodes.name: Fault report in
nodes.notes: One door for every channel. WhatsApp, the care inbox and the driver app all POST here, so the pipeline below is written once instead of three times.

nodes.name: Give the message an id
nodes.notes: Every channel is normalised here and nowhere else. Adding WhatsApp means adding a trigger and a second copy of THIS node; nothing downstream changes. inbound_id is the sender's own message id, and when a channel has none it falls back to a per-execution value, which means no replay protection for that channel - stated rather than faked.

nodes.name: Store it, or find the one we already have

parameters.query:
with existing as (
    select id, false as is_new
    from intake.report
    where channel = $1 and inbound_id = $2
), inserted as (
    insert into intake.report (channel, inbound_id, reporter, body, payload)
    select $1, $2, nullif($3, ''), $4, $5::jsonb
    where not exists (select 1 from existing)
    returning id, true as is_new
)
select * from inserted
union all
select * from existing

nodes.notes: Exactly one of the two CTEs produces a row, so this always returns one row and never updates anything - report stays insert-only. A true race (both copies inside one snapshot) makes the unique index raise, and the retry below finds the row on the second attempt: the retry IS the race handler. Measured against the on-conflict-do-update alternative, this also burns no sequence value on a replay.

nodes.name: Read the complaint

attributes.name: site
attributes.description: The charging site, exactly as the reporter named it. Do not expand, correct or guess a fuller name.

attributes.name: charger_label
attributes.description: The charger as the reporter named it, for example 'charger 3' or 'the DC one'. Leave empty if they did not say which charger. Never invent one.

attributes.name: symptom
attributes.description: What is wrong, in at most eight words, using the reporter's own meaning.

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Exactly one of: critical, high, normal, low. critical = unsafe or smoke or sparks. high = the charger cannot deliver energy at all. normal = it works but something is wrong. low = cosmetic, or a question.

attributes.name: confident
attributes.description: True only if the complaint names the site and the symptom unambiguously. False if anything had to be guessed.

attributes.name: note
attributes.description: What is missing or ambiguous in this complaint, for the human who may have to read it. Empty if nothing is.

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You are reading a fault report written by a site host, a driver or a technician, in whatever mixture of languages they use. Extract only what the text actually says.

You are NOT diagnosing the fault and you are NOT resolving the charger to an identifier in any system. A reader of your output must be able to check every field against the sentence they sent.

If the text does not say which charger, leave charger_label empty and set confident to false. An empty field is a correct answer. An invented one sends a technician to the wrong site.

nodes.notes: Each field's description IS the prompt for that field. severity is restricted to four words here as a request - and again in the database as a constraint, because only one of those two can actually refuse.

nodes.name: gpt-5-nano
nodes.notes: Reasoning effort low, deliberately. On the sibling RAG project reasoning was ~89% of the bill; reading one short complaint is not a task that needs it. A 30s timeout and two retries, because a hung call holds the webhook open.

nodes.name: Decide if a human must see it

assignments.name: report_id
assignments.value: ={{ $('Store it, or find the one we already have').item.json.id }}

nodes.notes: needs_human is OUR rule, not the model's opinion: unsure, or no charger named, or critical. The model is never asked this question, because it is already being asked whether it is confident - and two fields encoding one state is how the sibling project spent a whole day on a bug.

nodes.name: Store what the model made of it

parameters.query:
insert into intake.classification
    (report_id, model, site, charger_label, symptom, severity, confident, needs_human, note)
values ($1, $2, nullif($3, ''), nullif($4, ''), $5, $6, $7, $8, nullif($9, ''))
returning id, needs_human

nodes.notes: A new row per attempt, never an update. nullif() turns the model's empty strings into real NULLs, because 'absent' and 'the empty string' answer different questions and only one of them survives a WHERE clause. This is also where a fifth severity is rejected by the database.

nodes.name: Reply to the reporter

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "report": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id, "classification": $('Store what the model made of it').item.json.id, "ticket": $json.ticket_id, "ticket_opened": $json.ticket_opened === true, "escalated_to": $json.escalated_to || null, "severity": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity, "charger": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label, "symptom": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.symptom, "needs_human": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.needs_human, "note": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.note } }}

nodes.notes: Reached from two branches with two different item shapes, so everything but ticket_id, ticket_opened and escalated_to is read from a named node. needs_human is reported as the classification recorded it, not as a constant: on the attach branch it can be true while no human is ever told, and a reply that hides that is worse than the gap it hides. escalated_to is non-null only when this complaint raised the ticket it joined.

nodes.name: Is this a new message?
nodes.notes: true means nobody has sent us this message id before, so it goes to the model. false means the provider delivered it twice: the reply is still a 200 with the original report id, because arguing with a retrying webhook provider is a losing game - but the model is never called, so a replay costs nothing. Idempotency and cost control turn out to be the same mechanism here.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "report": $json.id, "duplicate": true, "note": "already received; nothing stored, no model call" } }}

nodes.name: Tell them we already have it
nodes.notes: The same 200 the first delivery got. A provider that reads anything other than 2xx will simply deliver a third time.

parameters.query:
select (
    select t.id
    from intake.ticket t
    where t.status = 'open'
      and lower(btrim(t.charger_label)) = lower(btrim($1))
      and coalesce(lower(btrim(t.site)), '') = coalesce(lower(btrim(nullif($2, ''))), '')
    order by t.opened_at
    limit 1
) as ticket_id

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.site }}

nodes.name: Find an open ticket for this charger
nodes.notes: Folds case and whitespace exactly as ticket_one_open_per_charger does - an index and a lookup that fold differently are two different questions, and the index always wins the argument. An empty charger_label matches nothing, which is correct: an unnamed charger cannot be deduplicated, and those complaints are exactly the ones a human has to read.

nodes.name: Already on a ticket?
nodes.notes: Deduplication sits BEFORE the approval gate on purpose. If the charger already has an open ticket, this complaint is more evidence for a fault we have already accepted - there is nothing for a human to decide and nobody new to dispatch. Putting it first is what keeps the review queue short.

parameters.query:
with existing as (
    select ticket_id, report_id, false as is_new
    from intake.ticket_report
    where report_id = $2
), linked as (
    insert into intake.ticket_report (ticket_id, report_id)
    select $1, $2
    where not exists (select 1 from existing)
    returning ticket_id, report_id, true as is_new
), joined as (
    select * from linked union all select * from existing
), escalated as (
    update intake.ticket t
       set severity = $3, symptom = $4
     where t.id = $1
       and array_position(array['low', 'normal', 'high', 'critical'], $3)
         > array_position(array['low', 'normal', 'high', 'critical'], t.severity)
    returning t.id, t.severity
)
select j.ticket_id, j.report_id, j.is_new,
       (select severity from escalated) as escalated_to
from joined j

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $json.ticket_id }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.symptom }}

nodes.name: Attach it to the open ticket
nodes.notes: Three complaints, one ticket - and the ticket now learns. A joining complaint whose severity outranks the ticket raises it; one that ranks lower changes nothing, so a cosmetic report can never quieten a critical ticket. Without this, a charger reported as sparking after being reported as tripping would sit at high for ever, and the dispatcher reads the ticket, not the reports. array_position over an ordered array is the ranking, because the four words have an order that text comparison does not know about.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.needs_human }}

nodes.name: Does a human have to approve?
nodes.notes: Only reaches here when no open ticket matched, so this is a fault we have not accepted yet. true means a person decides before anything is dispatched.

parameters.query:
with t as (
    insert into intake.ticket (site, charger_label, symptom, severity)
    values (nullif($1, ''), $2, nullif($3, ''), $4)
    returning id
), l as (
    insert into intake.ticket_report (ticket_id, report_id)
    select t.id, $5 from t
    returning ticket_id
)
select id as ticket_id, true as ticket_opened from t

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.site }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.symptom }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id }}

nodes.name: Open a ticket
nodes.notes: The confident, charger-named, not-critical path - no human needed. If two of these race, ticket_one_open_per_charger raises on the loser and the retry below re-runs the lookup, which by then finds the winner.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { "report": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id, "classification": $('Store what the model made of it').item.json.id, "status": "under review", "severity": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity, "charger": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label, "note": $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.note, "needs_human": true } }}

nodes.name: Tell them a human will look at it
nodes.notes: An acknowledgement, not an answer. The reporter cannot hold an HTTP request open while somebody reads their complaint, so the review branch replies now and does its work afterwards. The Wait node and the decision go after this node, not before it.

parameters.formTitle: ={{ 'Fault report ' + $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id + ' needs a decision' }}
parameters.formDescription:
={{ 'WHAT THEY SENT
' + $('Give the message an id').item.json.complaint + '

WHAT THE MODEL READ
site: ' + ($('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.site || '(none)') + '
charger: ' + ($('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label || '(none)') + '
symptom: ' + $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.symptom + '
severity: ' + $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity + '

WHY THIS STOPPED HERE
' + ($('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.note || 'the model was unsure, or called this critical') }}

values.defaultValue: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.site }}
={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.charger_label }}

options.formSubmittedText: Recorded. You can close this page.

nodes.name: Wait for a person to decide
nodes.notes: The execution is written to the database and sleeps here; submitting the form at /form-waiting/<executionId> wakes it. No thread is held, so a pending approval survives a container restart. This is the human task of a workflow engine, not a blocking call. It has no deadline, which is a known gap - an approval nobody opens waits for ever, and there is no reminder yet.

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: Everything that writes a ticket lives on the true side. That is what makes "a rejected approval leaves no side effects" a property of the shape of this workflow rather than a promise about its code.

parameters.query:
with d as (
    insert into intake.decision
        (report_id, decided_by, approved, reason, site, charger_label)
    values ($1, $2, true, nullif($3, ''), nullif($4, ''), $5)
    returning report_id, site, charger_label
), existing as (
    select t.id
    from intake.ticket t, d
    where t.status = 'open'
      and lower(btrim(t.charger_label)) = lower(btrim(d.charger_label))
      and coalesce(lower(btrim(t.site)), '') = coalesce(lower(btrim(d.site)), '')
    limit 1
), opened as (
    insert into intake.ticket (site, charger_label, symptom, severity)
    select d.site, d.charger_label, nullif($6, ''), $7 from d
    where not exists (select 1 from existing)
    returning id
), chosen as (
    select id, true as ticket_opened from opened
    union all
    select id, false from existing
), l as (
    insert into intake.ticket_report (ticket_id, report_id)
    select c.id, $1 from chosen c
    returning ticket_id
)
select id as ticket_id, ticket_opened from chosen

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id }}, {{ $('Wait for a person to decide').item.json.Reviewer }}, {{ $('Wait for a person to decide').item.json.Why }}, {{ $('Wait for a person to decide').item.json.Site }}, {{ $('Wait for a person to decide').item.json.Charger }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.symptom }}, {{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.severity }}

nodes.name: Record the approval and open or join a ticket
nodes.notes: The reviewer's site and charger win over the model's, because the model leaving charger blank is usually why this complaint stopped here at all. Symptom and severity still come from the model - the reviewer was asked to identify the charger, not to re-diagnose the fault.

parameters.query:
insert into intake.decision (report_id, decided_by, approved, reason)
values ($1, $2, false, nullif($3, ''))
returning id, approved

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id }}, {{ $('Wait for a person to decide').item.json.Reviewer }}, {{ $('Wait for a person to decide').item.json.Why }}

nodes.name: Record the rejection, and nothing else
nodes.notes: The only row a rejection writes. No ticket, no link, no message - and no charger either, even though the form collected one. This table is the gate itself, not a side effect of it: a review nobody can audit is indistinguishable from no review.

parameters.query:
insert into intake.pending_review (report_id, execution_id, review_url)
values ($1, $2, $3)
on conflict (report_id) do update
    set execution_id = excluded.execution_id,
        review_url   = excluded.review_url,
        queued_at    = now()
returning report_id, execution_id

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $('Decide if a human must see it').item.json.report_id }}, {{ $execution.id }}, {{ $execution.resumeFormUrl }}

nodes.name: Put it in the review queue
nodes.notes: Written BEFORE the reporter is told "under review", because saying it first and queueing second means a failed insert leaves a promise nobody can keep. $execution.resumeFormUrl carries the resume token n8n signs the waiting form with; without it the form answers 401, so this row is the only way anyone finds the gate. Read it through intake.review_queue, which drops a row the moment a decision exists - pending is derived, never stored.
